messages:
Alex: Quick Q re: timeouts/cancellation across SDKs — we need consistent expectations for AbortController (JS), context (Go), asyncio/requests (Python), and Java. What should abort do for streaming responses? Should client-initiated aborts avoid retries? Any guidance I'm missing?

Mike: Good question. TL;DR: explicit client cancel (AbortController.cancel / context cancel) should abort immediately and NOT trigger client retries. Retries should only apply for transient network/server errors. Example JS pattern:
```js
const controller = new AbortController();
const res = await fetch('/v1/generate', { signal: controller.signal });
// to cancel:
controller.abort();
// SDK: treat abort as user-cancelled, close stream, do not retry.
```

Sara: For Python sync requests we raise requests.exceptions.Timeout for client-side timeouts (these are often retriable depending on idempotency). For asyncio, a CancelledError should be raised when caller cancels, and streaming iterators need to stop iterating. Example (async):
```py
async def stream():
    try:
        async for chunk in client.stream(...):
            yield chunk
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        # propagate user cancel, don't trigger retry
        raise
```

Jordan: A couple of important details: 1) partial-stream behavior — if client aborts mid-stream, do we emit partial deltas or drop them? My recommendation: deliver any already-received deltas to the app, then close with a terminal 'aborted' marker. 2) server vs client timeouts mapping: client-initiated => 499-like, server processing timeout => 408/504. SDKs should map 499->no-retry, 408/5xx -> eligible for retry (if idempotent).

Alex: Good point. So canonical mapping we should document: client abort (client-side cancel or AbortController) => surface as a "client_cancelled" error/499, SDKs do NOT retry. Server-side processing timeouts => 408/504 (these may be retried per idempotency). Also need guidance on how retries interact with streaming calls and idempotency_key/header handling.

Mike: I'll add a spec section. Proposed bullets:
- AbortController / context cancellation: immediate stop, surface client_cancelled, no client retry.
- Network errors + 5xx + 408/504: allowed to retry based on idempotency policy.
- Streaming abort: SDK delivers already-received fragments then emits a final error frame with reason="client_cancelled".
- SDKs should expose a small helper to attach an idempotency key to streaming requests if the user wants resumable/retry semantics.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-specs/pull/42

ci-bot: deploy-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-specs/pull/42 — "abort-and-timeout-semantics"

Sara: I'll follow up with a Python SDK PR to raise CancelledError for user cancels and to document the mapping. Will add an async example using asyncio.wait_for + CancelledError.

Alex: Thanks all. @Mike @Sara let's sync after PRs land. Quick checklist for merge: spec text + SDK behavior + short examples in quickstart + one interop test asserting 499 mapping and that client cancels do not trigger retries. :thumbsup:
